record.paper_title: AUTOMORPHISMS AND DYNAMICS: A LIST OF OPEN PROBLEMS
record.context_brief: Invariant fibrations for birational maps of dynamical degree one
record.original_question: Let f be a birational transformation of a complex projective variety X with first dynamical degree λ_1(f) = 1. Does this condition force the existence of a non-trivial invariant fibration, meaning a dominant rational map π: X ⇢ B with 0 < dim(B) < dim(X) and a birational transformation f_B of B such that π ∘ f = f_B ∘ π?

evidence.quote: Instead of assuming that the entropy of f is zero, one may now assume that λ1(f) = 1, i.e. that degH(f n) does not grow exponentially fast with n.
One may also ask, as in Question 3.1, whether the equality λ1(f) = 1 implies the existence of a non-trivial invariant fibration.

By “non-trivial meromorphic fibration”, I mean that 0 < dim(B) < dim(X) and π is a dominant rational map; and f permutes the fibers of π if there is a birational transformation fB of B such that π ◦ f = fB ◦ π.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and let $f: X \dashrightarrow X$ be a birational transformation. Fix an ample divisor class $H$ on $X$, and define the first dynamical degree of $f$ by
$$\lambda_1(f) \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \bigl( (f^n)^* H \cdot H^{\dim X - 1} \bigr)^{1/n},$$
a quantity that does not depend on the choice of $H$ and is a birational invariant of $f$.

A non-trivial invariant meromorphic fibration for $f$ is a dominant rational map $\pi: X \dashrightarrow B$ to a (normal) projective variety $B$ with $0 < \dim B < \dim X$, together with a birational transformation $f_B: B \dashrightarrow B$, such that
$$\pi \circ f \;=\; f_B \circ \pi.$$

Question: Does $\lambda_1(f) = 1$ imply that $f$ admits a non-trivial invariant meromorphic fibration in the above sense?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the higher-dimensional setting. In dimension 2 it is known (work of Diller–Favre, Gizatullin, Cantat) that birational surface maps with $\lambda_1(f)=1$ and unbounded degree sequence preserve a rational or elliptic fibration. In higher dimensions the analogous statement is conjectural; related conjectures (e.g. the Zariski dense orbit conjecture for birational maps of dynamical degree one, arXiv:2202.06364) treat this regime as still open. No proof of the general higher-dimensional implication has been located.

status_evidence.title: A conjecture strengthening the Zariski dense orbit problem for birational maps of dynamical degree one
status_evidence.snippet: For a quasiprojective variety X with a birational self-map φ of dynamical degree 1, it is conjectured that either there exists a non-constant invariant rational function or a proper subvariety controlling all invariant subvarieties.
status_evidence.claim: The dynamical-degree-one regime is the subject of ongoing conjectures, indicating it is not settled in general.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical degrees of birational transformations of projective surfaces (Cantat)
status_evidence.snippet: When the degree grows linearly, the map preserves a rational fibration; quadratic growth yields an elliptic fibration.
status_evidence.claim: The surface case is resolved by preservation of a fibration, but higher dimensions are not addressed by these results.
